**Note:** This question can't be resolved yet. Q4 2026 runs Oct 1 to Dec 31, and Tesla normally publishes its Q4 delivery report around January 2. I didn't open the Metaculus FAQ page directly. Tesla's IR/SEC filings currently show results only through Q3 2026.

**Latest official data (Tesla 8-K, Oct 2, 2026)**
- Q3 2026: production 464,391; deliveries 486,532 (Model 3/Y 478,237; Other Models 8,295).
- That's up 1.3% from Q2's 480,126 and down 2.1% from Q3 2025's record 497,099. Q3 2025 had a buying rush before the US federal EV tax credit expired.
- It beat expectations by about 25,000, against Tesla's company-compiled consensus of 461,974 (24 analysts).
- Tesla delivered 22,141 more cars than it built. This was the second straight quarter of shrinking inventory, and Q2 and Q3 together cleared the roughly 50,000 excess vehicles built in Q1. So it has less spare inventory left to sell down in Q4.
- Year to date: 1,324,681 delivered through three quarters, up 8.8% from 1,217,902 at the same point in 2025.
- Other Models are shrinking: Model S and X production ended in January 2026, and Other Models deliveries are down 48% year over year.

(2024–2025 figures; 2026 figures from Tesla's 8-Ks above.)

Q4 compared with Q3: in 2024, Q4 was a record. In 2025, Q4 fell about 16% from Q3 because of the tax-credit cliff. Q4 2025 also missed Tesla's own consensus of 422,850 by about 1.1%, and Q1 2026 came in 2.1% under consensus. Q2 and Q3 2026 both beat by wide margins.

**Analyst expectations**
- At the end of September, the full-year 2026 consensus was raised to 1,767,255. That was read as implying about 467,100 in Q4, 11.7% more than a year earlier, but the calculation assumed Q3 would land at consensus.
- My own arithmetic: with the actual Q3 number, that unchanged full-year figure implies only about 442,600 in Q4. Expect the consensus to be revised after Q3's beat and tonight's earnings.
- I didn't find a live Kalshi or Polymarket price for Q4. For Q3, Kalshi traded in the low-to-mid 470,000s in late September, closer to the actual result than the Street was.

**Scheduled events before resolution**
- Today, Oct 21: Q3 2026 earnings after the close, with the Q&A webcast. Watch for Q4 or full-year guidance.
- Roadster event in Q4 (listed among upcoming events).
- Monthly registration data from China, Europe and elsewhere (Oct–Dec).
- Late December: Tesla posts its company-compiled Q4 consensus on its IR site.
- About Jan 2, 2027: Tesla's Q4 production and deliveries release, which resolves the question.

**Status quo:** The run rate is about 480,000–487,000 a quarter. A year-over-year comparison is easy because Q4 2025 (418,227) was depressed by the tax credit expiring. Working against Q4 are the depleted inventory buffer (Q3 production was only about 464,000) and the fading Other Models line.

criterios: This question resolves as the total number of vehicles Tesla delivered in Q4 2026, as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as the Tesla Investor Relations website (https://ir.tesla.com/press) or Tesla's SEC filings. The figure used is the total number of vehicles delivered (the sum of Model 3, Model Y, and Other models). For example, if Tesla reports 420,000 total deliveries, this resolves as 420000.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 weeks. Q4 ends December 31, and Tesla's production and deliveries release is expected around January 2, 2027.

(b) **If nothing changed:** The Q2–Q3 2026 run rate is about 480,000–487,000 a quarter, so Q4 would land near 485,000.

(c) **If the current trend continued:**
- **Seasonality pushes up.** Q4 normally beats Q3 because of the year-end push. In 2023, Q4 was 484,000 against 435,000 in Q3. In 2024, Q4 was 495,600 against 463,000.
- **Supply pushes down.** Q3 production was only about 464,000, and the inventory buffer is mostly gone after two quarters of drawdown. The fading Other Models line also subtracts a few thousand.
- **Net effect:** Roughly 470,000–500,000.

(d) **Experts and markets:**
- The late-September full-year consensus of 1,767,255 implied about 467,000 in Q4 if Q3 had come in at consensus.
- Using the actual Q3 figure, that same full-year number implies only about 442,600.
- After Q3 beat by about 25,000, revisions will probably push the Q4 expectation into the 465,000–490,000 range.
- Prediction markets were closer to the actual Q3 result than the Street was, but I found no live Q4 market price.

(e) **Low scenario:**
- Demand weakens in China or Europe, or competition intensifies.
- A production disruption occurs, such as a supply-chain shock or a factory retooling.
- With little inventory left to sell down, deliveries fall to 410,000–430,000.

(f) **High scenario:**
- A strong year-end push combines with incentives, cheaper model variants and robust Chinese demand.
- Production rises to around 500,000 or more and deliveries reach 520,000–540,000, approaching a record.

(a) **Time left:** About 10 weeks until Tesla is expected to report Q4 deliveries in early January 2027.

(b) **If nothing changed:** Q3’s delivery pace of 486,532 vehicles would put Q4 near 487,000. But Q3 deliveries exceeded production, so repeating that pace may require higher production rather than another inventory drawdown.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** Deliveries through Q3 are up 8.8% year over year. Applying that growth rate to Q4 2025 gives roughly 455,000 vehicles.

(d) **Experts and markets:** The cited full-year analyst consensus implies about 443,000 Q4 deliveries after accounting for the actual Q3 result, though that consensus predates Q3’s beat. No useful live Q4 market estimate was found.

(e) **Unexpected low scenario:** Production disruptions or weaker demand could pull deliveries toward 400,000.

(f) **Unexpected high scenario:** A strong year-end sales push paired with increased production could lift deliveries above 540,000.
